1926, September
FR. SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 1.
Page 33 Cont. Sept. 3rd Synobitis Cured Harold C. Byrne 11 of 656 Hall Ave., Windsor, Ont. fell July 30 his birth-day losing use of right leg complete- ly - leaving little hope of recovery. On August 4th is enrolled for year. The boy delerious till that time with fever and pain, remarked that something must have been done that he felt so im- proved. The Aunt who enrolled him phoned next morning to find wonderful improvement as said the doctor. To-day he comes with his Mother to the Monastery. Sept. 20th not worse: still has temperature.
May 1, 1927 Reported improving right along and in best of spirits.
Sept. 7th Mrs. Louise Knack 30, 356 So. Chalmers shot through head in hold up by burgelar and again through the arm, while in jewelry store, taken to receiving Hospital and found to have badly frac- tured scull, is enrolled June 30 same evening when recovery seemed entirely out of the question. Authorities in Hospital refuse all hope of recovery. "She is dying now," they said. "We can do absolutely nothing." In that extremity she is taken to other hospital where she received transfusion of blood (Deacon- ess Hosp. ). She leaves Hospit. in 11 days ... comes to Monas- tery this evening, with
Oliver Gamache 40, 10692 W. Jefferson (365 lbs) heart-failure on account of fat and asthma enrolles 2nd time to-day - dropsey - & bronchitis
Blind Baby. Philip Moceri 10 months, soft brain & blind etc enrolled To-day.
Sept. 10th Mrs. Clara Rousseau 46, of 192 Elmhurst Ave. Highland Pk. fearing examination for inward cancer enrolles doubly To-day, promising frequent communion if ----
Page 34 Sept. 10 Cancerous Brain Tumer Cured? Joseph Ryan 41, Union Town Pa. to have operation on brain tumer is enrolled night before opera- tion Feb - 23 The doctors finding fearful tumer as about the brain and cancerous sews up incision in scalp and scull - 35 stitches - giving him one month to become entirely blind and in- sane. To-day Sept. 10 reported improving, after 7 months, Tumer seems to be going away, the patient who has a wife and three small children believes operation went off O.K. & successful - Dr. Temple Fay of Philadelphia marveled principal operater mar- veled when he saw him come to his office; --- Dec. 7th Reported as "set back" seemingly by repetition of x Ray June 14 '27 Fearfully suffering .... yet going to daily Comn.
